catalog_quote: [p.545] For the description of the Palaung word it is necessary to distinguish two types of syllable, which will be referred to as major and minor syllables. ... a major syllable is one which contains a vowel, a minor syllable containing no vowel other than an anaptyctic one, represented in the transcription by ə. With the exception of a small number of loanwords, and of the proolitic particles mentioned in the next paragraph, all Palaung words consist of a major syllable which may be preceded by one or two minor syllables. Symbolizing major syllables by (Ma) and minor ones by (Mi), the possible structures are thus : Monosyllable (Ma) e.g. ta? ' to weave ' Disyllable (MiMa) e.g. korta? 'tongue' Trisyllable (MiMiMa) e.g. rekerta? 'loom ' ... There are in Palaung a number of proclitio particles which consist of a minor syllable only, e.g. ke (loh) ' (does) not (go) '. sweep_summary: Shwe Palaung (shwe1236) is in the catalog as fixed-unreviewed (final/major-syllable prominence, Shorto 1960). The sweep's two Glottolog title-hits — Butt, Bögel & Jabeen 2017 (LFG'17, open PDF fetched sources and read: Urdu/Hindi polar kya, 0 mentions of Palaung) and Butt, Jabeen & Bögel 2020 (De Gruyter, DOI 10.1515/9783110650532-004, paywalled; title names Urdu/Hindi) — are both mis-linked to shwe1236: Glottolog's records state the language link is a 'computerized assignment from "kya"'. Both are other-language items, silent on the catalog, priority none. Semantic Scholar API returned 429; a Crossref title query for 'Palaung stress' surfaced no new stress source beyond Shorto 1960 (the catalog's own deciding source) plus non-stress Palaung items (Ostapirat-era 'Dara'ang Palaung' handbook chapter DOI 10.1163/9789004283572_024 is a different variety and not a stress title). No change to the catalog coding is warranted. fetched sources

audit.reasoning: (1) All three deciding loci (Shorto 1960 p.545 word template, p.546 n.2 stress definition, p.556 'major syllable probably always carries more stress than the minor syllable') are present verbatim (scanned noise only) in the held text at the stated pages; the Milne 1921 p.12 contra line and the loanword exception passage are also confirmed. (2) The coding rests on a phonology article devoted to word/syllable structure of exactly this variety; the held Mak 2012 reference grammar is consistent (pre-syllable vowel always reduced to schwa) but silent on stress; identity of Shorto/Milne/Mak's variety as Namhsan Ta-ang = shwe1236 is confirmed by the newly fetched sources Deepadung et al. 2015. the only unheld phonological work touching Gold Palaung is an unpublished 1978 conference paper.
